/-!
# Bloch and Landau constants

*References:*
- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bloch%27s_theorem_(complex_analysis))
- [CP96] Chen, H., Gauthier, P. M. "On Bloch's constant." Journal d'Analyse Mathématique 69 (1996),
  275–291.
- [AG37] Ahlfors, L. V., Grunsky, H. "Über die Blochsche Konstante." Mathematische Zeitschrift 42
  (1937), 671–673.
- [Ya95] Yanagihara, H. "On the locally univalent Bloch constant." Journal d'Analyse Mathématique
  65 (1995), 1–17.
- [Ra43] Rademacher, H. "On the Bloch-Landau Constant."" American Journal of Mathematics 65 (1943),
  387–390.
- [OptimizationConstants](https://teorth.github.io/optimizationproblems/constants/57c.html)
- [Skin2009] Skinner, Brian. The univalent Bloch constant problem. Complex Variables and Elliptic
  Equations 54 (2009), no. 10, 951–955.
- [MathWorld](https://mathworld.wolfram.com/BlochConstant.html)
- [Bhowmik–Sen](https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/canadian-mathematical-bulletin/article/improved-bloch-and-landau-constants-for-meromorphic-functions/FD465D1F2CEF7E8C62AFF16C3E89B7B4)
- [Re2008] Rettinger, R. ["Bloch's constant is computable."](https://jucs.org/jucs_14_6/blochs_constant_is_computable/jucs_14_06_0896_0907_rettinger.pdf)
  Journal of Universal Computer Science 14 (2008), 896–907. In particular, a schlicht disk is the
  image of a subdomain under a biholomorphic restriction.
-/

@[expose] public section

open scoped Topology ENNReal
open Metric Set Filter
namespace Bloch

/-- The **Bloch radius** $B_f$ of a function $f$ is the supremum of radii of schlicht disks in the
image of the unit disk under $f$: the restriction of `f` maps an open subdomain injectively and
onto the disk. Requiring an open subdomain and equality of the image is essential; mere containment
would allow an arbitrary set-theoretic choice of one preimage per point. Takes values in `ℝ≥0∞` so
that functions whose image contains arbitrarily large schlicht disks correctly get radius `⊤`
rather than `0`. -/
noncomputable def blochRadius (f : ℂ → ℂ) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  sSup (ENNReal.ofReal '' {r : ℝ | ∃ S, IsOpen S ∧ S ⊆ ball (0 : ℂ) 1 ∧
    ∃ x, f '' S = ball x r ∧ InjOn f S})

@[category API, AMS 30]
lemma zero_le_blochRadius (f : ℂ → ℂ) : 0 ≤ blochRadius f := zero_le

@[category API, AMS 54]
lemma dis_add_radius_le_of_ball_subset_ball {X 𝕜 : Type*} [RCLike 𝕜] [NormedAddCommGroup X]
    [NormedSpace 𝕜 X] [Nontrivial X] {x y : X} {r d : ℝ} (hpos : 0 < r) (hsub : ball x r ⊆ ball y d) :
    dist x y + r ≤ d := by
  have : Tendsto (fun s => dist x y + s) (𝓝[<] r) (𝓝 (dist x y + r)) :=
      (tendsto_nhds_of_tendsto_nhdsWithin tendsto_id).const_add _
  refine le_of_tendsto this ?_
  filter_upwards [Ioo_mem_nhdsLT hpos] with t ⟨hl, hr⟩
  by_cases! hxy : x = y
  · obtain ⟨v, hv⟩ := exists_ne (0 : X)
    simp_all only [dist_self, zero_add]
    let u := (‖v‖⁻¹ : 𝕜) • v
    have : ‖u‖ = 1 := by apply norm_smul_inv_norm; grind
    calc
    _ = ‖y + (t : 𝕜) • u - y‖ := by simp_all [norm_smul, abs_of_nonneg hl.le]
    _ ≤ d := by
      refine (mem_ball_iff_norm.1 (hsub (mem_ball_iff_norm.2 ?_))).le
      simp_all [norm_smul, abs_of_nonneg hl.le]
  · let u := (‖x - y‖⁻¹ : 𝕜) • (x - y)
    have : ‖u‖ = 1 := by apply norm_smul_inv_norm; grind
    calc
    _ = ‖x - y‖ + t := by
      simp [NormedAddCommGroup.dist_eq]
      rw [← norm_neg (-x  + y)]
      simp [add_comm, sub_eq_add_neg]
    _ = ‖x + (t : 𝕜) • u - y‖ := by
      simp [u, add_sub_right_comm, ← smul_assoc]
      nth_rw 2 [← one_smul 𝕜 (x - y)]
      rw [← add_smul, norm_smul]
      norm_cast
      rw [abs_of_nonneg (by positivity), add_mul, one_mul, mul_assoc, inv_mul_cancel₀ (by aesop),
        mul_one]
    _ ≤ d := by
      refine (mem_ball_iff_norm.1 (hsub (mem_ball_iff_norm.2 ?_))).le
      simp_all [norm_smul, abs_of_nonneg hl.le]

@[category API, AMS 54]
lemma radius_le_of_ball_subset_ball {X 𝕜 : Type*} [RCLike 𝕜] [NormedAddCommGroup X]
    [NormedSpace 𝕜 X] [Nontrivial X] {x y : X} {r d : ℝ} (hpos : 0 < r)
    (hsub : ball x r ⊆ ball y d) : r ≤ d :=
  trans (by simp) (dis_add_radius_le_of_ball_subset_ball (𝕜 := 𝕜) hpos hsub)

@[category API, AMS 30]
lemma blochRadius_id_eq_one : blochRadius id = 1 := by
  apply le_antisymm
  · -- blochRadius id ≤ 1: every valid radius r satisfies r ≤ 1
    apply sSup_le
    rintro _ ⟨r, ⟨S, -, hS, x, hball, -⟩, rfl⟩
    simp only [image_id] at hball
    by_cases hpos : 0 < r
    · exact (ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal
        (radius_le_of_ball_subset_ball (𝕜 := ℂ) hpos (hball ▸ hS))).trans
        (by simp [ENNReal.ofReal_one])
    · exact (ENNReal.ofReal_of_nonpos (by linarith)).le.trans zero_le
  · -- 1 ≤ blochRadius id: ball 0 1 ⊆ id '' ball 0 1
    rw [show (1 : ℝ≥0∞) = ENNReal.ofReal 1 from by simp]
    exact le_sSup ⟨1, ⟨ball (0 : ℂ) 1, isOpen_ball, Subset.rfl, 0, by simp⟩, rfl⟩

/-- The **Landau radius** $L_f$ of a function $f$ is the supremum of radii of disks contained in
the image of the unit disk under $f$. Takes values in `ℝ≥0∞` so that functions with unbounded
image correctly get radius `⊤`. -/
noncomputable def landauRadius (f : ℂ → ℂ) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  sSup (ENNReal.ofReal '' {r : ℝ | ∃ x, ball x r ⊆ f '' (ball (0 : ℂ) 1)})

/-- The **Bloch constant** $B$ is the largest radius such that every holomorphic function on the
unit disk with $f'(0) = 1$ has a schlicht (univalent) disk of that radius in its image. -/
noncomputable def blochConstant : ℝ :=
  sSup {B : ℝ | ∀ f : ℂ → ℂ, DifferentiableOn ℂ f (ball 0 1) → deriv f 0 = 1 →
    ∃ S, IsOpen S ∧ S ⊆ ball 0 1 ∧ ∃ x, f '' S = ball x B ∧ InjOn f S}

/-- It is proved in [CP96] that the Bloch constant is bounded below by
$\sqrt{3}/4 + 2 \times 10^{-4}$ -/
@[category research solved, AMS 30]
theorem blochConstant_lower_bound : Real.sqrt 3 / 4 + 2 * 10 ^ (-4 : ℤ) ≤ blochConstant := by
  sorry

/-- It is proved in [AG37] that the Bloch constant is bounded above by
$\frac{1}{\sqrt{1 + \sqrt{3}}}\frac{\Gamma(1/3) \Gamma(11/12)}{\Gamma(1/4)}$. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 30]
theorem blochConstant_upper_bound :
    blochConstant ≤ Real.Gamma (1 / 3) * Real.Gamma (11 / 12) /
    (Real.Gamma (1 / 4) * Real.sqrt (1 + Real.sqrt 3)) := by
  sorry

/-- Ahlfors and Grunsky also conjectured in [AG37] that this upper bound is the precise value of the
Bloch constant. -/
@[category research open, AMS 30]
theorem blochConstant_exact_value :
    blochConstant = Real.Gamma (1 / 3) * Real.Gamma (11 / 12) /
    (Real.Gamma (1 / 4) * Real.sqrt (1 + Real.sqrt 3)) := by
  sorry

/-- The **Univalent Bloch constant** $B_u$ is the largest radius such that every univalent
holomorphic function on the unit disk with $f'(0) = 1$ has a schlicht disk of that radius in its
image. -/
noncomputable def univalentBlochConstant : ℝ :=
  sSup {B : ℝ | ∀ f : ℂ → ℂ, InjOn f (ball 0 1) → DifferentiableOn ℂ f (ball 0 1) →
    deriv f 0 = 1 → ∃ S, IsOpen S ∧ S ⊆ ball 0 1 ∧
      ∃ x, f '' S = ball x B ∧ InjOn f S}

/-- It is proved in [Skin2009] that the Univalent Bloch constant is bounded below by $0.5708858$. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 30]
theorem univalentBlochConstant_lower_bound : 0.5708858 ≤ univalentBlochConstant := by
  sorry

/-- The Univalent Bloch constant is trivially bounded above by the Bloch radius of the identity
function, which is $1$. This is the best upper bound we know according to [OptimizationConstants]. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 30]
theorem univalentBlochConstant_upper_bound : univalentBlochConstant ≤ 1 := by
  apply csSup_le
  · -- the set is nonempty: 0 is in it (ball x 0 = ∅ ⊆ anything)
    exact ⟨0, fun f _ _ _ => ⟨∅, isOpen_empty, empty_subset _, 0, by simp⟩⟩
  · -- every B in the set is ≤ 1
    intro B hB
    have h := hB id (injOn_id _) differentiableOn_id (by simp)
    rcases h with ⟨S, -, hS, x, hball, -⟩
    simp only [image_id] at hball
    by_cases hpos : (0 : ℝ) < B
    · exact radius_le_of_ball_subset_ball (𝕜 := ℂ) hpos (hball ▸ hS)
    · linarith

/-- The **Landau constant** $L$ is the largest radius such that every holomorphic function on the
unit disk with $f'(0) = 1$ has a disk of that radius contained in its image. -/
noncomputable def landauConstant : ℝ :=
  sSup {B : ℝ | ∀ f : ℂ → ℂ, DifferentiableOn ℂ f (ball 0 1) → deriv f 0 = 1 →
    ∃ x, ball x B ⊆ f '' (ball 0 1)}

/-- It is proved in [Ya95] that the Landau constant is bounded below by $0.5 + 10 ^ {-335}$. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 30]
theorem landauConstant_lower_bound : 0.5 + 10 ^ (-335 : ℤ) ≤ landauConstant := by
  sorry

/-- It is proved in [Ra43] that the Landau constant is bounded above by
$\frac{1}{\sqrt{1 + \sqrt{3}}}\frac{\Gamma(1/3) \Gamma(5/6)}{\Gamma(1/6)}$. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 30]
theorem landauConstant_upper_bound :
    landauConstant ≤ Real.Gamma (1 / 3) * Real.Gamma (5 / 6) / Real.Gamma (1 / 6) := by
  sorry

/-- In [Ra43], Rademacher says that he strongly believed that this upper bound is the precise value
of the Landau constant. -/
@[category research open, AMS 30]
theorem landauConstant_exact_value :
    landauConstant = Real.Gamma (1 / 3) * Real.Gamma (5 / 6) / Real.Gamma (1 / 6) := by
  sorry

end Bloch

findings.description: The docstring gives Rademacher's upper bound as $\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+\sqrt{3}}}\frac{\Gamma(1/3)\Gamma(5/6)}{\Gamma(1/6)}$. The Lean statement (correctly) is `landauConstant ≤ Real.Gamma (1/3) * Real.Gamma (5/6) / Real.Gamma (1/6)`, with no factor $1/\sqrt{1+\sqrt3}$; that factor belongs to the Ahlfors–Grunsky Bloch bound and was copied over. Numerically, the docstring expression is ≈ 0.32867 while the Lean expression is ≈ 0.54326 (computed with a Lanczos Gamma). 0.3287 is below the known L > 1/2, so the docstring's formula cannot be an upper bound. The next docstring (`landauConstant_exact_value`, "this upper bound") inherits the slip. The Lean mathematics is right.
findings.source_evidence: Wikipedia (Bloch's theorem (complex analysis)): "0.5 < L ≤ Γ(1/3)Γ(5/6)/Γ(1/6) = 0.543258965342...". MathWorld Landau Constant: "Robinson (1938, unpublished) and Rademacher (1943) derived the bounds 1/2 < L ≤ Γ(1/3)Γ(5/6)/Γ(1/6) = 0.5432589...". OptimizationConstants 57b, quoting Bhowmik–Sen 2023: "1/2+10^{-335} < L ≤ Γ(1/3)Γ(5/6)/Γ(1/6) ≈ 0.5433".
findings.suggested_fix: Change the docstring to: "It is proved in [Ra43] that the Landau constant is bounded above by $\frac{\Gamma(1/3)\Gamma(5/6)}{\Gamma(1/6)} \approx 0.5433$." Leave the Lean statement unchanged.

findings.description: The docstring says the trivial bound 1 (from the identity map) "is the best upper bound we know according to [OptimizationConstants]". The OC 57c page does list only the trivial bound, so the attribution is literally accurate, but the claim is false. The file's own Wikipedia reference gives A ≤ 0.7853 for injective functions. The map artanh z = ½log((1+z)/(1−z)) is univalent with f'(0)=1 and maps onto the strip |Im w| < π/4, which gives B_u ≤ π/4 ≈ 0.785. The literature has ≈ 0.6564. The Lean statement `univalentBlochConstant ≤ 1` is true and proved in the file; only the docstring is affected.
findings.source_evidence: Wikipedia (Bloch's theorem (complex analysis)): "For injective holomorphic functions on the unit disk, a constant A can similarly be defined. It is known that 0.5 < A ≤ 0.7853". zbMATH review of Beller–Hummel (Complex Variables 4 (1985) 243–252): improves "die bisherige obere Schranke für die schlichte Bloch-Konstante von A<0.6564681 (Goodman 1945) auf A<0.6564155". zbMATH review of Carroll–Ortega-Cerdà (2009), "The univalent Bloch-Landau constant, harmonic symmetry and conformal glueing": 𝒰 ≤ 0.6563937.
findings.suggested_fix: Reword, e.g.: "The univalent Bloch constant is trivially at most the Bloch radius of the identity, which is $1$. Much better upper bounds are known (e.g. $\pi/4$ from the strip map, and $0.6563937$ by Carroll–Ortega-Cerdà)." Consider tagging the proved trivial bound `textbook` rather than `research solved`.

reformulations.difference: Lean defines B = sSup {r : every f with DifferentiableOn ℂ f (ball 0 1) and deriv f 0 = 1 has an open S ⊆ ball 0 1, injective on S, with f '' S = ball x r}. That is a sup of radii attained uniformly by all f. The sources (Bhowmik–Sen / OC 57a, MathWorld, Rettinger) define B = inf_{f∈F} B_f, where B_f is the sup of radii of univalent disks of f. The sources also differ in normalization details: Ω a *domain* (connected) mapped univalently onto the disk (BS2023); a subregion S with f(S) ⊇ disk (MathWorld); |f'(0)| = 1 on the closed disk (Wikipedia); f(0)=0, f'(0)=1 on a neighbourhood of the closed disk (MathWorld).
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For each f in F the set R_f of schlicht radii is down-closed: if f '' S = ball x r, then S ∩ f⁻¹(ball x r') is open (f is continuous on the disk) and maps injectively onto ball x r'. R_f also contains every r ≤ 0 (take S = ∅), and ⋂ R_f is bounded above by 1 (f = id). Hence sSup ⋂_f R_f = inf_f sup R_f. I proved this in Lean (/workspace/review/reform.lean, axioms propext/choice/Quot.sound only): `ENNReal.ofReal blochConstant = ⨅ f : {f : ℂ → ℂ // DifferentiableOn ℂ f (ball 0 1) ∧ deriv f 0 = 1}, blochRadius f`. The remaining differences are standard (argued, not in Lean). Connectedness of S is automatic: f injective and holomorphic on S is open, so S ≅ ball. Containment reduces to equality by restricting S to f⁻¹(disk). Rotation turns |f'(0)|=1 into f'(0)=1. Translation handles f(0)=0. Scaling f(ρz)/ρ with ρ→1 shows the open-disk and closed-disk classes give the same infimum.

reformulations.difference: Lean defines L = sSup {r : every f in F has some ball x r ⊆ f '' ball 0 1}. The sources define L = inf_{f∈F} L_f, with L_f the radius of the largest disk in f(D) (Wikipedia, MathWorld, OC 57b).
reformulations.equivalence_argument: R_f = {r : ∃ x, ball x r ⊆ f(D)} is down-closed and contains 0, and the intersection is bounded by 1 via id. So sSup ⋂ R_f = inf_f sup R_f. Proved in Lean: `ENNReal.ofReal landauConstant = ⨅ f : {f // DifferentiableOn ℂ f (ball 0 1) ∧ deriv f 0 = 1}, landauRadius f`. The normalization differences (|f'(0)|=1, closed disk, f(0)=0) are handled by rotation, scaling and translation as for B.

reformulations.difference: Lean defines B_u as sSup of radii r such that every univalent f in F has a schlicht disk of radius r. The source (BS2023 / OC 57c) defines B_u = inf{B_f : f ∈ F univalent}. Skinner, Carroll–Ortega-Cerdà and Wikipedia's A use the inradius of f(D) for univalent f, i.e. the univalent Bloch–Landau constant.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Same down-closure argument. Proved in Lean: `ENNReal.ofReal univalentBlochConstant = ⨅ f : {f // InjOn f (ball 0 1) ∧ DifferentiableOn ℂ f (ball 0 1) ∧ deriv f 0 = 1}, blochRadius f`. For univalent f every disk in f(D) is schlicht (take S = D ∩ f⁻¹(disk)), so B_f equals the inradius L_f, and this is the univalent Bloch–Landau constant of the literature.

sources_consulted: Bhowmik–Sen, Improved Bloch and Landau constants for meromorphic functions, Canad. Math. Bull. 66 (2023), PDF from cambridge.org (text partially extracted; digits garbled, cross-checked against OC quotes)
Rettinger, Bloch's constant is computable, J.UCS 14 (2008) 896–907, PDF from https://www.jucs.org/jucs_14_6/blochs_constant_is_computable/

zbMATH Open reviews (api.zbmath.org): Chen–Gauthier 1996; Yanagihara 1995 (bound 1/2+10^{-335} is for the locally univalent Bloch constant B_l ≤ L); Ahlfors–Grunsky 1937 (conjectured exact value); Bonk 1990; Beller–Hummel 1985; Carroll–Ortega-Cerdà 2009; Jenkins 1998

review.notes:
I checked all declarations. All three constants are faithful to the sources. I proved in Lean (sorry-free, /workspace/review/reform.lean) that each sSup-form definition equals the source's inf_{f∈F} of the per-function radius, using the file's own `blochRadius`/`landauRadius`. The bound statements match the literature. Numerically (Lanczos Gamma): Ahlfors–Grunsky ≈ 0.4718617, Rademacher ≈ 0.5432590, Chen–Gauthier ≈ 0.4332127. The literals elaborate as exact reals: 0.5708858 = 5708858/10^7, 10^(-4:ℤ) is real zpow.

Skinner's abstract states the univalent lower bound as 0.5708858. BS2023 gives B_u > 0.5708858, so `0.5708858 ≤ univalentBlochConstant` is supported.

Yanagihara (1995) proved 1/2 + 10^{-335} for the locally univalent Bloch constant B_l. The Landau bound follows since B_l ≤ L: lift through the universal covering of f(D). BS2023 and OC also attribute the Landau lower bound to him, so the docstring attribution is acceptable.

Status: both exact-value conjectures (Ahlfors–Grunsky for B, Robinson/Rademacher for L) are still recorded as unproved (OC pages, BS2023), so `research open` is correct. The bound theorems are correctly `research solved`.

Cosmetic, not reported: the reference key [CP96] should be [CG96] (Chen–Gauthier), and there is a stray double quote in the [Ra43] entry.

I could not open the full texts of Chen–Gauthier, Ahlfors–Grunsky, Rademacher or Yanagihara (the Springer/JSTOR pages sit behind bot challenges). Every bound is confirmed by several independent secondary sources (MathWorld, Wikipedia, BS2023, Rettinger, zbMATH reviews).
